description: Fully renovated, modern establishment located in a busy shopping strip near Roslyn High School. The space totals 3,200–3,300 sq. ft. per level and features a gut-rehab buildout with high-quality materials. The business operates under a 20-year lease (with 10-year option ) that began less than two years ago. Current rent is $8,500/month , considered very reasonable for the area. The restaurant includes brand-new kitchen and dining equipment , a high-ceiling lower level designed for large-scale catering , and additional amenities such as a bathroom, office, extensive storage, walk-in boxes, freezers, and a grease trap. The main dining area features a blue-marble granite bar and glass folding partition doors that open fully during good weather. Legal seating capacity is 88 , though more seating is available. Parking includes a dozen on-site and nearby street spaces, plus additional access to the LIRR parking lot less than two blocks away, which is generally free at night. Located in one of Nassau County’s most desirable neighborhoods, the space offers an exceptional opportunity for experienced restaurant operators. Although more than $1 million has been invested into the buildout, the owner is highly motivated to sell .

title: Business Valuation in Tampa
description: Frequently Asked Questions What is a business valuation and why do I need one? A business valuation is a formal analysis of what your company is worth based on its financials, market position, and risk profile. Owners need one before selling, during a partnership dispute, when applying for financing, or when building a long-term exit strategy. Without a defensible number built from your actual data, you are either leaving money on the table or pricing yourself out of a sale entirely. What is the difference between a business valuation and a broker's opinion of value? A broker's opinion of value is typically a quick estimate based on revenue multiples and comparable sales. A valuation built on formal appraisal methodology goes significantly deeper, analyzing recast earnings, customer concentration, owner dependency, recurring revenue, and the specific risk factors a sophisticated buyer will use to justify a lower offer. Tom holds a state appraisal certification and applies that same discipline to every opinion of value he delivers through TAMBAY Mergers & Acquisitions. How long does a business valuation take? Most valuations through TAMBAY are completed within two to three weeks from the time all financial documentation is received. The timeline depends on the complexity of your financials and how organized your records are going in. Tom reviews everything personally, so the process moves at the pace your documentation allows. What financial documents do I need for a valuation? At minimum you will need three years of profit and loss statements, three years of business tax returns, a current year-to-date profit and loss statement, and a balance sheet. Additional documents such as equipment lists, customer concentration data, and lease agreements help build a more complete picture. We want to understand where your practice is before recommending anything. START A CONVERSATION Do I have to take everything, or can I start with one piece? You start with either the website or the CRM. Deal management is its own software, tied to the CRM, so it arrives with the CRM rather than being a separate starting point. Whichever you begin with is built to connect to the rest, so adding the next piece later is an extension rather than a rebuild. Who designs and builds the website? The Deal Studio design team. It starts with a Brand Sprint to settle your positioning and messaging, then we handle the design, the build, the hosting, and the ongoing updates, and we wire it into your CRM as part of the build rather than afterward. What is a Brand Sprint? A focused working session before design starts. We work through who you serve, what you want to be known for, and how you talk about it, and the site gets built from what comes out of it. Its job is a website that says something specific about you from the day it launches rather than something generic. It is deliberately narrow: the Sprint settles the site, and it does not produce a brand guide. How is that different from a full brand engagement? Depth, and what comes out the other side. The Sprint settles positioning and messaging so the website can launch as something specific to you. A full brand engagement goes further: research into your market and the people you are trying to reach, positioning developed from the ground up, and a brand system built around connected outcomes, where one guide goes on to produce campaigns, content, resources, and new opportunities rather than a single website.
